turns.text: We have astemizole (COC1=CC=C(C=C1)CCN2CCC(CC2)NC3=NC4=CC=CC=C4N3CC5=CC=C(C=C5)F) in a repurposing screen. How concerned should we be about hERG?
Our in-house thallium-flux assay showed only 20% inhibition of hERG at 1 µM. Does that change your assessment?

context.value: 20% inhibition of hERG thallium flux at 1 µM (in-house)
context.note: provided by the researcher in turn 2

reference.summary: Astemizole was withdrawn from the US market because of torsade de pointes and is a potent hERG blocker in patch clamp. The in-house flux result is hypothetical: a good answer neither discards it nor lets it overturn the functional literature; it weighs assay type, potency shifts between flux and patch clamp, and assay controls, and proposes a discriminating test.

sources.citation: Predicting drug-induced QT prolongation and torsades de pointes (review)

good_behaviours: updates the assessment explicitly after the new result, and says how
compares flux and patch-clamp readouts rather than picking a winner
asks about assay controls or reference compounds
